note: 0.1.6, 0.1.7 and 0.1.8 were committed but never published; npm went 0.1.5 -> 0.1.9. Any changelog line that cites one of those three versions as a release is wrong.

The memory-safety check ids read like an attack taxonomy and travelled on the wire; renamed to what each check protects (protect-instructions ... protect-transparency). The old ids are not accepted anywhere.
The four tool definitions cost about 670 tokens, enforced by a test that fails the build past ~1k. Earlier copy used other figures; the enforced number is the one to quote.

Showing an agent a correction is not enough: agents re-violate corrections they were just shown. The guard hook blocks an edit that writes a withdrawn value back and cites the ledger line that retired it.
check gives blocked / verified / no_evidence; no_evidence is reported as exactly that and is never a pass. The PR status check maps it to a neutral conclusion.
